# Catalog entries no feature-coverage scene uses yet, one "<kind> <name>" per
# line. `test_tools --feature-coverage` fails when a catalog entry is missing
# from both the scenes and this list, and when a listed entry becomes used.
# A feature PR covers its new entries in a scene; list one here only under a
# comment that gives the reason (a blank line ends a group), and remove lines
# as scenes start using them.

# Native compiler helpers Text Byte Length, Text Byte At, Text Slice and Text
# Bytes are exercised by the package-core language fixture. Text From Bytes is
# exercised by package-portable's authored byte tests and native ownership cases.
# These uncategorized pure declarations are excluded by feature_function, so no
# function gaps apply here.

# Material simulation: fluids, destruction worlds, heat and combustion need a
# material field and solver scene.
component MaterialFluidWorld
component MaterialDestructionWorld
component MaterialBreakProfile
component MaterialThermal
component MaterialConstitutive
component MaterialTerrain
component TerrainVolume
component Combustion
component Fuel
component Igniter
component MaterialCavity
component FragmentGlow
component MaterialFrame
component FluidVolume

# 2D lighting and sky.
component HRC2D
component Starfield2D

# Visibility queries: the rendering scene authors fog and a vision source but
# does not query sight from a behavior.
function Visibility At

# Combat, encounters and pickups: gameplay modules a combat scene would cover.
component Weapon
component Projectile
component SpawnRequest
component Encounter
component EncounterMember
component Experience
component Pickup
function Count Matching Entities

# Engine internals that scenes don't author directly.
component Drive

# The private tool.build catalog is deliberately absent from game/scene hosts.
# build-process and build-toolchain exercise all of its file, text, environment,
# argument and process capabilities on bytecode and SLJIT; scene admission would
# expose build authority to games. No runtime capability entries are omitted.

# The application, program, project and SDK catalogs belong to standalone
# application hosts and are absent from the deployed game catalog. Ordinary
# CLI, program-session and SDK boundary tests exercise those services with
# their explicit bindings. Their filesystem/process/network capabilities are
# host authority, not scene entries, so no function gaps are listed here.

# Compiler JSON String belongs only to the private compiler catalog. The
# package-routes-chibi differential exercises its decoded value and lifetime
# through authored routing on both backends; it is absent from scene catalogs.

# Compiler Syntax Parse belongs only to the private compiler catalog. The
# package-snapshot-chibi differential compares its raw trees and detached
# lifetimes on both backends. Scene catalogs do not expose compiler services.

# Move Objects is a Studio-host service rather than a runtime catalog entry.
# Studio's OutlinerInput uses it; --outliner-move exercises its authored drop
# event and scene-move covers the scene contract. It cannot run in this fixture.

# External browsing requires an opted-in interactive host and real user input.
# Source-native-features tests the authored requests without launching websites.
function Open URL
function Cancel Open URL

# Terrain checkpoints need a terrain recipe and host-bound binary storage.
# --terrain-playable exercises all three from .chibi in VM and SLJIT;
# --terrain-storage and --terrain-storage-commands cover storage failures.
function Save Terrain
function Load Terrain
function Terrain Storage Result
